unit.unitOverview:
Name the places in a town.
Stop a person politely and ask the way.
Understand left, right and straight on.
Check the answer before you go.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: places and directions.
Patterns: excuse me, where is, and turn left.
Listen to three short texts.
Ask the way. Record it.
Write directions to your home.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Name the places in a town
Stop a person politely with excuse me
Understand left, right and straight on
Check an answer by saying it back
Ask a person to slow down or repeat

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 13. Finding a place.
This unit is for the street.
First, places. Listen.
A shop. A market. A school. A bank.
A street. A bus stop. A station.
Say them with me.
Now the most important two words today.
Excuse me.
You say them before you ask a stranger.
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Say it with me. Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Now the answer. Three directions.
Left. Right. Straight on.
Say them with me. Left. Right. Straight on.
Turn left. Turn right. Go straight on.
And two more words.
The corner. It is on the corner.
Far. Is it far? No, it is near.
Now the part people forget.
You must CHECK the answer.
They say: turn left at the corner.
You say: turn left at the corner? Thank you.
Say the answer back. Every time.
If it was fast, say: slowly, please.
If you did not hear, say: again, please.
That is Unit 13. Go and ask the way.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Excuse me, where is...?
grammar.explanation:
Two parts. The excuse me matters as much as the question.
Without it, you sound like you are giving an order.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Excuse me. Where is the station, please?

Excuse me  +  Where is the ___  +  please

For more than one: Where ARE the toilets?
grammar.workedExample:
You are lost and you need the station.
1. Wait until the person looks at you.
2. Say: Excuse me.
3. Then: Where is the station, please?
4. Listen to the whole answer.
5. Then say it back to check.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not start with the question alone.
Where is the bank? with no excuse me sounds sharp.
Two words fix it.
grammar.memoryTip: Excuse me first. Please at the end.
grammar.practice:
Ask for each place.
1. the bank
2. the station
3. the market
4. the toilet
grammar.answerKey:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please? and so on.
Check: excuse me at the start of all four?
Check: please at the end?

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Left, right, straight on
grammar.explanation:
Three answers cover most directions.
Learn them with your hands, not your eyes.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Turn left.
Turn right.
Go straight on.

It is on the left.
It is on the right.
It is on the corner.

turn = change direction
go straight on = do not turn
grammar.workedExample:
Someone says: turn left at the corner.
1. Find the corner first.
2. Then turn left there.
3. Point with your hand as they speak.
4. That fixes it in your head.
5. Then say it back to check.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not nod without understanding.
Point with your hand instead.
If your hand is wrong they will tell you.
grammar.memoryTip: Use your hand while they talk.
grammar.practice:
Turn, go or on?
1. ___ left at the bank.
2. ___ straight on.
3. It is ___ the right.
4. ___ right at the corner.
grammar.answerKey:
1. Turn
2. Go
3. on
4. Turn
All four? You can follow a direction now.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Say it back
grammar.explanation:
This is the half of the lesson people skip.
Asking is easy. Understanding the answer is the hard part.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
They say:  Turn left at the corner.
You say:   Turn left at the corner? Thank you.

They say:  It is on the right, next to the bank.
You say:   On the right, next to the bank? Thanks.
grammar.workedExample:
You asked and they answered fast.
1. Do not say thank you and walk away.
2. Say the main part back.
3. Your voice goes up, like a question.
4. They will say yes, or they will fix it.
5. Now you can go.
grammar.commonMistake:
A nod is not checking.
Nod when you were wrong, and you go wrong.
Saying it back takes three seconds.
grammar.memoryTip: Say it back, then thank them.
grammar.practice:
Say each answer back.
1. Turn left at the bank.
2. Go straight on to the corner.
3. It is on the right.
4. It is next to the market.
grammar.answerKey:
1. Turn left at the bank?
2. Straight on to the corner?
3. On the right?
4. Next to the market?
All four? This one habit will save you many wrong turns.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Can you show me?
grammar.explanation:
Unit 3 gave you again and slowly, for words.
In a street you have a better move.
Ask for the answer in another FORM.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Can you show me?        (they point, or walk with you)
Can you write it, please?
Can you show me on the map?

Words are hard. A hand and a map are not.
grammar.workedExample:
They gave directions and you caught nothing.
1. Asking again gives you the same words.
2. So change the form instead.
3. Say: Sorry. Can you show me?
4. Most people point, or walk a few steps with you.
5. Still unsure? Say: Can you write it, please?
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not ask for the same words three times.
The third time will sound the same as the first.
Ask to SEE it instead.
grammar.memoryTip: A hand beats a sentence when you are lost.
grammar.practice:
What do you say?
1. You want them to point. ___
2. You want it on paper. ___
3. You have a map with you. ___
4. You want the street name written. ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. Can you show me?
2. Can you write it, please?
3. Can you show me on the map?
4. Can you write it, please?
All four? You have a way out when words fail.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: The checking half matters more than the asking half
teacherNotes.note: Most courses teach the question and stop. A learner who asks well and then cannot follow the answer is no better off. Pattern 3 and Practice 4 are the ones that change what happens in the street. Do not skip them for time.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Teach left and right with hands, not words
teacherNotes.note: A learner translating left in their head while somebody talks will lose the rest of the sentence. Get them pointing as the other person speaks. A wrong hand gets corrected on the spot, which is exactly what you want.

teacherNotes.noteType: Excuse me is a whole move
teacherNotes.note: Wait to be looked at, say excuse me, ask, listen, say it back, thank them. Practise the sequence, not the phrase. A learner who has done it six times in a room will do it once in a street.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Asking twice is the skill, not a failure
teacherNotes.note: Many adults will walk away lost rather than ask a second time. Say plainly that asking again is normal and that native speakers do it constantly. That sentence is worth as much as the vocabulary.
